authority: Current official Android documentation read with web tool; source summaries are requirements input, not runtime evidence
inference: Touch mode is a plausible unobserved fixture precondition in the failed run, not an established product cause.

sources.finding: Screen input enters touch mode; directional input exits it. Touch-mode focus requires isFocusableInTouchMode. Mode persists across windows and activities and is queried using isInTouchMode.
sources.title: Input events overview: Touch mode and Handling focus

sources.finding: A focus request can fail for non-focusability, touch-mode restrictions, invisibility or ancestor FOCUS_BLOCK_DESCENDANTS. getDescendantFocusability exposes the ancestor policy.
sources.title: ViewGroup requestFocus and descendantFocusability

sources.finding: sendKeySync targets the currently focused window and waits for event handling; display reaction can continue afterwards, so native idle and actual state remain separate observations.
sources.title: Instrumentation sendKeySync

sources.finding: The public global-mode setup API requires the originating process to have internal MODIFY_TOUCH_MODE_STATE on Android 13 and later; shell has that permission. Selected fixture uses ordinary directional navigation input instead.
sources.title: Instrumentation setInTouchMode

sources.finding: Navigation DOWN can be consumed before Activity dispatch when leaving touch mode selects focus. An absent Activity DOWN alone is not evidence of consumption.
sources.title: Official framework checkForLeavingTouchModeAndConsume

sources.finding: The public callback reports whether the view hierarchy is now in touch mode after a mode change.
sources.title: Public touch-mode observer
